checked_claims.note: Re-derived. Twisting the two-term CE resolution by O_X(2) and using R^j p_* O_X(-2)=0 (the first negative higher image on a P^2-bundle occurs at t<=-3) gives F=p_*(I_C(2)) and the short exact sequence 0->F->Sym^2 E->gamma_* R->0. Rank/degree: deg(Sym^2 E)=(r+1)deg E=36, chi=42; chi(R)=31 under (N); hence chi(F)=11 and deg F=9. The identification R tensor gamma^*O(-6)=L^{tensor 2} uses the strong form of (N). On P^1, F=O(s)+O(9-s) with s<=4 gives h^0(F(-6))=4-s, vanishing iff s=4. Target dimension 7 is Riemann-Roch for a degree-12 bundle with h^1=0, independent of further geometry.

Re-derived. A smooth plane quintic is neither hyperelliptic nor trigonal (base-point-free pencil trick against |H|). Every g^1_4 is then |H-p_0|: a non-complete pencil of degree 4 would give a g^2_4 and Clifford equality, already excluded. Thus L=H+p_0 has p_0 as a base point, h^0(D)=2 forces a_i>=2, h^0(2D)=h^0(omega-2p_0)=4 forces sum (3-a_i)_+=1, hence E=O(2)+O(3)+O(4). The four monomials with a_i+a_j>=6 all vanish to order at least 2 at p_0 (ord xi_4=2, ord xi_3>=1), so the 7-dimensional source maps into H^0(2H) of dimension 6.

If p is a base point then |D+p| is a g^2_5. A further base point produces a g^2_4 and Clifford equality, hence a hyperelliptic fibre, excluded by ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2. A base-point-free g^2_5 is birational onto a plane quintic of arithmetic genus 6, necessarily smooth, excluded by CLM-0103-2. This supplies the degree-zero case left open by ATT-0088/CLM-0088-4 and matches FND-0130, with the missing classification of g^1_4's included.

Re-derived. H^0(L)=t^*H^0(O(2)) is an isomorphism of 3-dimensional spaces. The case h^0(4T-omega)=1 produces D~2T-A of degree 2 and, in every configuration of A relative to t, either h^0(D)=1 or a base point of |D|, contradicting that D=gamma^*O(1) is a complete base-point-free pencil. Then h^0(2D)=3 forces E=O(3)^3, so res is the multiplication map Sym^2 H^0(L)->H^0(L^{tensor 2}) with image inside the 5-dimensional t^*H^0(O(4)). No Maroni/Hirzebruch input is used. Compatible with a balanced (1,2)-(2,2) complete intersection having the same E but a different H^0(L).

deg phi_L divides 6 and deg X_L>=2. Degree 6 is degenerate; degree 3 is a smooth conic, hence L=T^{tensor 2}, excluded by CLM-0103-4; a singular cubic has geometric genus 0, so the normalization would make C hyperelliptic (alternatively h^0(L)>=4). The remaining degree-2 case is a smooth plane cubic: Riemann-Hurwitz gives deg M=5, omega_C=psi^*M, D=psi^*P with P in Pic^2(Y), and |D|=psi^*|P| because h^0(P-M)=0. Lemma 1(1) at m=1,2 forces E=O(2)+O(3)+O(4). Hyperelliptic fibres are already excluded by the imported CLM-0088-2; plane quintics by CLM-0103-2.

The incidence I is a P^1-bundle over C, hence irreducible, so monodromy is transitive. After deleting the diagonal and the finite coincidence locus Sigma over non-normal points of the sextic, the ordered-pair incidence is irreducible of dimension two and dominant of generic degree 30, so monodromy is 2-transitive, hence primitive. A general tangent line is a simple tangency at a smooth point of the dual curve (char-0 reflexivity of the Gauss map; Wronskian of the g^2_6 has degree 48 and is not identically zero because the system is not composed with a pencil), giving local monodromy a transposition via the comparison of etale and topological fundamental groups in characteristic zero. Jordan's theorem yields S_6. The writeup incorrectly equates connectedness of the S_6-torsor with transitivity on six letters (A_6 would already be transitive while giving two components); that slip is not load-bearing, because G=S_6 is already established and connectedness of Ord is equivalent to G=S_6 by FND-0148/FND-0151.

On a reduced member, j^*l consists of three distinct non-branch points of psi, and phi_L^*l is the disjoint union of the three fibres. The partition is independent of the line, so it is monodromy-invariant. The corresponding imprimitive wreath product has order 2^3*3!=48 and is not S_6. The exact image inside the wreath product is not claimed.

Existence of (Y,P,M,B) is elementary (four values of M excluded; |M^{tensor 2}| is very ample of degree 10, so Bertini gives a reduced member). Smoothness, connectedness and genus six of C, and finite-flatness of gamma, are immediate. The splitting E=O(2)+oplus O(3)-oplus O(4)- follows from q_*O_Y=O+O(-2) and q_*M=O(1)+O(2), matched against gamma_*omega_C=O(-2)+E(-2) with omega_{P^1} even. The restriction map is iota-equivariant of rank 7=6+1; the odd summand sends x_2 x_4 to a nonzero multiple of mu. Injectivity of the even map Phi is the pole/trace argument: f=nu/mu is a rational section of P with a single simple pole at y_0, hence not iota-invariant because y_0 is unramified; a=0 would make f a pullback; a!=0 produces a quadratic for F=f/tau over q^*k(P^1) whose trace has a simple pole at q(y_0) while c_1/(a c) is regular there. Lemma 1(4) therefore gives (BAL). Hypotheses (CE) and (N) are not reproved; they are imported exactly by the FND-0150-sanctioned pair CE 1996 Theorem 2.1 plus SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, which SRC-0004 itself cites as [15, Theorem 2.1(2)] for the restriction O(1)|_C cong omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2). Criterion (3.3) of ATT-0100 is not used.

U->S is smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two with connected fibres |L_s|^{rs}, so U_alpha is connected. The closed fibre U_b sits in U_alpha and carries the restricted S_6-torsor, so im(pi_1^{et}(U_b)->S_6) is contained in H_alpha. That fibrewise image is S_6 by CLM-0103-6, hence H_alpha=S_6. Connectedness of Z_alpha is then the single-orbit case of FND-0148/FND-0151. The upgrade from connected to irreducible retains the normality/integrality/locally-Noetherian hypothesis demanded by FND-0132. The induction functor of FND-0152 with H_alpha=S_6 is the identity. No irreducibility of S is used, and no statement is made about a purely type-(ii) component. k algebraically closed makes the arithmetic/geometric distinction of FND-0148 vacuous.

finding_candidates.statement: Evidence for FND-0130, with the missing classification of pencils supplied. If L=omega_C(-D) had a base point p on a balanced+(N) genus-six degree-four fibre, then |D+p| is a g^2_5. A further base point of that system produces a g^2_4 and Clifford equality, hence a hyperelliptic fibre, excluded by ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2 and FND-0125. A base-point-free g^2_5 is birational onto a plane quintic of arithmetic genus 6, necessarily smooth. On a smooth plane quintic every g^1_4 is |H-p_0| (non-completeness would again give a g^2_4), so L=H+p_0 has p_0 as a base point, E cong O(2)+O(3)+O(4), and H^0(Sym^2 E(-6))->H^0(L^{tensor 2}) has seven-dimensional source with image inside the six-dimensional H^0(omega_C), hence h^0(F(-6))>=1, contradicting (BAL). Thus L is base-point-free on the balanced locus. The new load-bearing steps are the identification of every g^1_4 as |H-p_0| and the vanishing-order computation at p_0.

hypotheses: L base-point-free of degree 6 with h^0=3

finding_candidates.statement: Under (CE)+(BAL)+(N) at genus six, after L is known to be base-point-free, the finite morphism phi_L:C->P^2 onto an irreducible nondegenerate plane curve satisfies deg(phi_L)*deg(X_L)=6 and exactly one of two cases occurs. Type (i): deg phi_L=1 and X_L is a plane sextic with normalization C. Type (ii): deg phi_L=2, X_L is a smooth plane cubic Y, psi=phi_L is a bielliptic double cover with psi_*O_C=O_Y+M^{-1}, deg M=5, omega_C=psi^*M, L=psi^*O_Y(1), gamma=q o psi with q=phi_{|M tensor O(1)^{-1}|} of degree two, and E cong O(2)+O(3)+O(4). The excluded alternatives are deg phi_L in {3,6}, a singular cubic image (normalization P^1, hence C hyperelliptic), a smooth plane quintic, and L cong T^{tensor 2} for a base-point-free g^1_3. The trigonal exclusion is a section count: it forces E cong O(3)^3 and lands the balancedness restriction map inside the five-dimensional pullback t^*H^0(O(4)), so h^0(F(-6))>=1. Downstream arguments that need phi_L birational must impose type (i) explicitly; primitivity of gamma is not available on the whole balanced locus.

hypotheses: (CE) and (N) supplied by Casnati-Ekedahl 1996 Theorem 2.1 and SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6

finding_candidates.statement: A non-primitive degree-four pencil factoring through a smooth genus-one intermediate curve can have balanced Casnati-Ekedahl splitting F cong O(4)+O(5). For every elliptic Y, every P in Pic^2(Y), every M in Pic^5(Y) whose unique point y_0 with O(y_0) cong M tensor P^{-2} is not a ramification point of q=phi_{|P|}, and every reduced B in |M^{tensor 2}|, the double cover psi:C->Y branched along B is a smooth connected genus-six curve and gamma=q o psi is finite flat of degree four with E cong O(2)+O(3)+O(4) and F cong O(4)+O(5), once (CE) and (N) are imported by the FND-0150-sanctioned pair CE 1996 Theorem 2.1 and SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6. Such data exist. Consequently primitivity of gamma is not a property of the balanced locus, and the residual question of FND-0104 is answered affirmatively for intermediate genus one. The argument does not treat intermediate genus two or three, does not assert that a connected component of a balanced base can be purely of type (ii), and does not compute the exact monodromy image inside S_2 wr S_3.

hypotheses: type (i) geometric fibre, or a connected component of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base meeting the type-(i) locus
normality of U_alpha for irreducibility and for the FND-0152 identity

finding_candidates.statement: On a balanced type-(i) geometric fibre the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs})->S_6 is the full symmetric group: the point-line incidence is an irreducible P^1-bundle (transitivity); after deleting the diagonal and the finite coincidence locus over non-normal points of the sextic, the ordered-pair incidence is irreducible and dominant of degree 30 (2-transitivity, hence primitivity); a general tangent line is a simple tangency at a smooth point of the dual curve (a transposition, using characteristic-zero reflexivity of the Gauss map and nonvanishing of the Wronskian of the complete g^2_6); Jordan's theorem then gives S_6, so the ordering torsor is connected. Over any connected component S_alpha of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base that contains at least one type-(i) geometric fibre, functoriality of pi_1^{et} along U_b -> U_alpha forces H_alpha=S_6, hence Z_alpha is connected; if U_alpha is additionally normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible, [S_6:H_alpha]=1, and the FND-0152 induction functor is the identity. This computes the monodromy image left open by FND-0148 and FND-0152, but only on components that meet the type-(i) locus. In type (ii) the image lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6. The statement upgrades nothing to Tate type (FND-0053, FND-0152(ii)), does not apply to algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144), and does not determine H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) component.

strongest_attack: The strongest attack is the FND-0150 circularity attack on the existence clause (E), and it fails. Clause (E) asserts that an explicit bielliptic-composed cover is balanced. The same pattern that FND-0150 used to leave ATT-0100/CLM-0100-12 unresolved is: construct a smooth genus-six degree-four cover, then invoke a balancedness criterion that was derived only under (CE)+(N), without constructing or citing the Casnati-Ekedahl embedding, the two-term resolution, or the restriction in (N). Here the attack is that Lemma 1(4) (BAL iff the restriction H^0(Sym^2 E(-6))->H^0(L^{tensor 2}) is injective) is itself derived under (CE)+(N), so applying it to the constructed cover cannot produce (BAL) unless (CE)+(N) are independently supplied. The attack fails because the theorem does not hide this: (CE) and (N) are imported by the source-backed pair SRC-IN-1, which is exactly Casnati-Ekedahl 1996 Theorem 2.1 (relative-canonical embedding and two-term resolution for every finite flat Gorenstein cover of degree d>=3) plus SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 / [15, Theorem 2.1(2)] (O(1)|_C cong omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2)). That is the discharge FND-0150 explicitly authorises. Balancedness is then proved from scratch by an iota-eigenspace computation and a pole/trace argument that never invokes ATT-0100 (2.1) or (3.3). The y_0-unramified hypothesis is used, and is necessary for the non-invariance of f=nu/mu. Secondary attacks that were run and also failed: (1) connectedness of Ord(|L|^{rs}) is written as equivalent to transitivity on six letters, which is false (A_6 is transitive while giving two components), but G=S_6 is independently established by 2-transitivity plus a simple-tangency transposition plus Jordan, so connectedness follows from the correct criterion G=S_6; (2) family monodromy in (F) cannot be read from a single special fibre — it can, because U_b = |L_b|^{rs} is a closed subscheme of U_alpha and the restricted torsor realises fibrewise monodromy as a subgroup of H_alpha; (3) stack-versus-coarse, integral-versus-rational, cohomology-versus-Borel-Moore, Poincare/Tate bookkeeping, Gysin/Kunneth shifts, spectral-sequence differentials, Aut-invariants versus coinvariants, semisimplification versus a Hodge isomorphism, predicted motives as theorems, silent Tate-to-tautological upgrades, and omitted stable pairs all miss, because (A)-(F) assert no map to M_{6,6}, no stack descent, no integral or coarse statement, and no Hodge, weight, purity or Tate conclusion. Confirming the lemma does not verify RED-0001 and does not compute H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) component.
theorem_statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, C a smooth projective connected curve of genus 6 over k, and gamma: C -> P^1 a finite flat morphism of degree four, with gamma_*O_C = O_{P^1} + E^vee (E of rank three and degree nine), Casnati-Ekedahl embedding i: C -> X = P(E^vee), p: X -> P^1, p_*O_X(1) = E. Assume (CE) the ideal of i has the standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl resolution 0 -> O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F -> O_X(-2) tensor p^*F -> I_C -> 0 with F of rank two; (N) O_X(1)|_C is isomorphic to omega_C tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(2); and (BAL) F is isomorphic to O_{P^1}(4) + O_{P^1}(5). Put D = gamma^*O_{P^1}(1) and L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D), of degree six with h^0(L) = 3. THEN: (A) L is base-point-free, so phi_L: C -> P^2 is a finite morphism onto an irreducible nondegenerate plane curve X_L with deg(phi_L)*deg(X_L) = 6. (B) Exactly one of two cases holds. Case (i): deg(phi_L) = 1 and X_L is a plane sextic with normalization C. Case (ii): deg(phi_L) = 2 and X_L is a smooth plane cubic; writing Y = X_L and psi = phi_L: C -> Y, the curve Y is elliptic, psi is a bielliptic double cover with psi_*O_C = O_Y + M^{-1}, deg M = 5, omega_C = psi^*M, L = psi^*N with N = O_{X_L}(1) of degree three, E is isomorphic to O(2)+O(3)+O(4), and gamma = q o psi where q = phi_{|P|}: Y -> P^1 is the degree-two morphism attached to P = M tensor N^{-1} in Pic^2(Y); in particular gamma is non-primitive and factors through a curve of genus one. The remaining possibilities do not occur: deg(phi_L) is never 3 or 6, X_L is never a singular cubic, C is never hyperelliptic and never a smooth plane quintic, and L is never the square of a base-point-free degree-three pencil. (C) In case (i), let |L|^{rs} be the open subset of |L| = P^2 of divisors with six pairwise-distinct points and Ord(|L|^{rs}) -> |L|^{rs} the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings. Then Ord(|L|^{rs}) is connected and the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs}) -> S_6 is the full symmetric group S_6. (D) In case (ii), the fibres of psi cut each divisor of |L|^{rs} into three blocks of size two, and this partition is monodromy-invariant; hence the monodromy image lies in the imprimitive wreath subgroup S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6. (E) Case (ii) is nonempty. Let Y be an elliptic curve over k, P in Pic^2(Y) with degree-two morphism q = phi_{|P|}: Y -> P^1, M in Pic^5(Y) such that the unique point y_0 with O_Y(y_0) isomorphic to M tensor P^{-2} is not a ramification point of q, and B in |M^{tensor 2}| reduced; let psi: C -> Y be the double cover branched along B. Then C is smooth connected of genus six, gamma = q o psi is finite flat of degree four, and (C,gamma) satisfies (BAL). Such data exist, and (CE) and (N) hold for every such (C,gamma) by the source-backed input SRC-IN-1. Hence the balanced locus contains tetragonal pencils factoring through a genus-one intermediate curve. (F) Let S be a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme carrying a genus-six degree-four family satisfying (CE), (BAL) and (N) on every geometric fibre, AJ = P_S(pi_*L), U the reduced-support open of AJ, and Z = Ord(U) -> U the finite etale S_6-torsor of orderings of ATT-0088 (III). If S_alpha is a connected component of S over which some geometric fibre is of type (i), then the geometric monodromy image H_alpha of pi_1^{et}(U_alpha) -> S_6 equals S_6; consequently Z_alpha is connected, and if U_alpha is in addition normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible, the component index [S_6 : H_alpha] equals one, and the S_6-induction functor of FND-0152 is the identity. No Hodge, weight or Tate conclusion is asserted anywhere in (A)-(F).
